80428.subject: Bitcoin Falls Below Its $84,000 Cost Basis
80428.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Bitcoin](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-holds-below-84000-cost-basis-level-nine-of-125-tokens-rise-oct-07-2026)**[ fell below its $84,000 cost-basis level](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-holds-below-84000-cost-basis-level-nine-of-125-tokens-rise-oct-07-2026)

* **[Moody's](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/moody-s-rates-sky-b3-flagging-thin-capital-buffer)**[ rated Sky B3 and flagged its thin capital](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/moody-s-rates-sky-b3-flagging-thin-capital-buffer)

* **[BitMine](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/bitmine-will-stop-buying-eth-at-5-of-supply-tom-lee-says)**[ will stop buying ETH at 5% of supply](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/bitmine-will-stop-buying-eth-at-5-of-supply-tom-lee-says)

* **[Polymarket](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/coplan-stops-short-of-mentioning-a-polymarket-token-at-token2049)**['s Coplan named no token or date at TOKEN2049](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/coplan-stops-short-of-mentioning-a-polymarket-token-at-token2049)

* **[Hyperliquid](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/hyperliquid-confirms-singapore-base-but-says-it-has-no-mas-license)**[ has a Singapore base but no MAS license](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/hyperliquid-confirms-singapore-base-but-says-it-has-no-mas-license)

Research desks spent the week naming $84,000 as bitcoin's support level. Bitcoin has traded below it since late Tuesday. On Wednesday only nine of the 125 largest tokens rose.

**Bitcoin** fell in two legs. Late Tuesday it [fell 2.1% in about 20 minutes on Coinbase, to $83,551](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-sinks-below-84-000-in-sudden-sell-off), and Coinalyze counted $83 million of bitcoin long liquidations. At Wednesday's U.S. open it [fell again, to $82,717](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-holds-below-84000-cost-basis-level-nine-of-125-tokens-rise-oct-07-2026), on the heaviest hourly volume of the session. No exchange, protocol or regulator announced anything in either window. Bitcoin traded at $83,181 at 6 p.m. ET, down 2.9% on the day. Also on Wednesday, **BitMine** chairman Tom Lee [said the company will stop buying ETH at 5% of supply](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/bitmine-will-stop-buying-eth-at-5-of-supply-tom-lee-says).

The Federal Reserve [raised rates by a quarter point on Sept. 16](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-round-trips-fed-rate-increase-zcash-sep-16-2026), its first increase since 2023. Bitcoin [reached $86,355 on Sept. 21](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-highest-since-january-crude-sinks-sep-21-2026), its highest price since January, and two days later it [fell back through the $86,000 ETF cost basis](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-eases-etf-creations-1-7-billion-sep-23-2026). 80425.subject: 🟪 Crypto can originate-and-distribute now
80425.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e7522d88-0d94-40c3-aca0-ac3a4cccbf6c/Stellar_BD-Banner-Sponsor_Template.png?t=1790361050)
Follow image link: (https://meridian.stellar.org/register)
Caption: 

----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3bd8a492-ff61-41db-a7f2-c821d481fd72/BD_NL_QuoteCircle.png?t=1781794162)
Caption: 

“A bank is therefore not an office for ‘borrowing’ and ‘lending’ money, but it is a Manufactory of Credit.”
_— _Henry Dunning Macleod, _The Theory of Credit_ (1891)



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9ebba5db-2577-471b-ad32-ffd7ba734e57/image.jpeg?t=1791342916)
Caption: 

**Crypto can originate-and-distribute now**

Roughly speaking, there are three ways a bank can make money from deposits.

One: _clip coupons_. 

We accept low or no interest on our bank deposits in return for the convenience of having a checking account to receive a paycheck into and pay bills out of. Banks can make money by investing those deposits in risk-free government debt (or parking them with the Fed). Banks that do _only_ this are called “100% reserve” or “narrow” banks. There are not many modern examples, in part because the Fed discourages it (they want banks making loans). 

A notable exception is stablecoin issuers. Circle, for example, is a narrow bank: it has all [$77 billion](https://s206.q4cdn.com/265218871/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/Q1-2026-Earnings-Presentation-1.pdf) of its deposits (the dollars it’s received in return for USDC) invested in cash and cash equivalents. Tether is an almost-narrow bank: it has 75% of its [$189 billion](https://assets.ctfassets.net/vyse88cgwfbl/2kYf7r64h3tzwiu6F0CbUB/2997abd2f11ecea74a21528048b50707/Opinion___Report_-_Tether_International_Financial_Figure_30-06-2026.pdf) of assets in cash and cash equivalents (the rest is in a mishmash of bitcoin, gold, equities, and loans).

Two: _originate and hold_. 

This is the model that most people think of when they think of banks: taking deposits and making loans. 

(Or _creating_ deposits by making loans. It depends how you look at it.) 

Traditional banks like the Bailey Brothers Building and Loan would simply hold the loans they make until maturity, earning a spread on the difference between what they pay depositors and what they charge borrowers. This had the benefit of making banks think hard about what loans it should make. It also had the disbenefit of creating duration mismatch — the short-dated liabilities (on-demand deposits) and long-dated assets (mortgages, say) that make banks subject to runs.
